$description: DESY light theme — the DESY corporate palette (DESY Styleguide 06/24) using officially published hexes only, on a white-forward canvas per the styleguide's external-communications rule ('higher proportion of white with the DESY branding elements in their standard colours'). The terminal surface is DESY White; page backgrounds are the light end of the interpolated `petrol` neutral ramp (derived from DESY dark blue #004a6e — the canvas is the one non-published element, since four official neutrals cannot express five surface tiers plus three text tiers). Because the styleguide's palette is print-derived, its bright half (yellow, olive, light-green, turquoise, orange, brand cyan) is not AA-legible on a near-white page, so every text-bearing slot here draws from the dark half: Black, Dark blue, Purple, Aubergine, Petrol, Dark red, Magenta. accent.base is the official accessibility cyan #007bc8 with DESY Black as accent.on — black clears 4.67:1 on it where white scores 4.4995:1, which is what previously forced an off-styleguide nudge; the nudge is now gone. KNOWN AA SHORTFALL: accent-secondary resolves to DESY accessibility orange #eb6e0f at 2.90:1 on bg.primary, below all three WCAG tiers. This is a deliberate brand constraint, not an oversight — DESY publishes no darker orange, and engineers #eb6e0f to the 3:1 non-text floor on pure white (3.10:1) rather than the 4.5:1 text floor its cyan counterpart hits, i.e. the styleguide treats orange as a graphics colour on light backgrounds. accent-secondary.light collapses onto its base for the same reason. The desy family therefore drops the accent-secondary.light gate in gates_for_family(); every other AA gate passes vs bg.primary (#f3f8fc): text.primary 9.02:1, text.secondary 5.61:1, text.muted 3.40:1, accent 4.21:1, accent.on (black on cyan) 4.67:1.

terminal.$description: DESY White terminal surface — the styleguide's 'higher proportion of white'.

base.$description: DESY accessibility cyan #007bc8, the official styleguide hex — 4.21:1 on bg.primary, clearing the 3:1 non-text gate this slot is held to.

light.$description: Collapsed onto accent.base. The styleguide's other cyan is the brand #009fdf, which is *lighter* (2.80:1 here) and so cannot serve as a higher-contrast emphasis slot on a light canvas. Under the official-hexes-only rule there is no third cyan to interpolate.

on.$description: DESY Black on accent.base fills — 4.67:1, clearing the 4.5:1 gate. White would score 4.4995:1 and fail; using the styleguide's own black instead of a nudged cyan keeps every brand hex intact.

base.$description: DESY accessibility orange #eb6e0f — the styleguide's prescribed on-screen orange for light backgrounds, at 2.90:1 on this canvas.

light.$description: Collapsed onto accent-secondary.base, and the theme's one accepted AA shortfall. The only other published orange (#f18f1f) is lighter still at 2.26:1, and DESY publishes no darker orange at all — the styleguide tunes this hex to the 3:1 non-text floor on white, so it is a graphics colour by design, not a text colour. Consumers that need legible secondary-accent text on this theme should use text.primary and reserve orange for fills, borders and markers.

hover.$description: DESY brand orange #f18f1f as the brighter hover, mirroring the main light theme's lighter-than-base hover.

success.$description: DESY Green #00a54b — 3.03:1, the non-text tier; the palette has no darker green.

warning.$description: DESY accessibility orange #eb6e0f at 2.90:1. DESY Yellow (1.47:1) and Olive (1.91:1) are far worse on a near-white canvas, and Dark olive (3.61:1) reads as green rather than as a warning, so the accessibility orange remains the best-semantics official choice here.

error.$description: DESY Dark red #b92d41 — 5.59:1, the palette's strongest true red on light.

error-hover.$description: DESY Red #eb5a2d at 3.26:1. The palette has no red deeper than Dark red, so the hover brightens rather than deepens here.

accent.$description: Alpha composite of the accessibility cyan (#007bc8).

neutral.$description: Base rgb(111,138,155) = color.petrol.500 = text.muted's exact color — the petrol step at ~the same relative lightness as the main light theme's gray.500 neutral-tint base.

overlay.$description: Same hand-tuned light-mode overlay alphas as the main light theme (non-monotonic values preserved there for fidelity; kept identical here for cross-theme consistency).

error-dialog.$description: Error glow recomputed from DESY Dark red.

diff.$description: Add/delete washes and text recomputed from the DESY Green/Dark red pair rather than the main light theme's generic green/red.

selection.$description: Alpha composite of the accessibility cyan. The previous solid pale-cyan #d6effa was an interpolated tint and is not a published hex, so the selection is now an alpha wash of the official colour instead.

ansi.$description: ANSI slots drawn from the DESY secondary palette's dark half, which is the only half legible on a near-white canvas. Normal/bright pairs run dark -> light here, the inverse of the dark theme (dark-red 5.59 -> red 3.26; green 3.03 -> light-green 2.27; dark-olive 3.61 -> olive 1.91; dark-blue 8.91 -> petrol 5.83; aubergine 6.42 -> magenta 4.95; accessibility cyan 4.21 -> brand cyan 2.80). The bright variants of the warm/green slots are weak by construction — DESY's bright graphic colours are built for white paper as fills, not as foreground text.

bright-cyan.$description: The brand cyan #009fdf as the bright variant.

chart.$description: Paper/plot = bg.primary and grid/axis = the text.secondary family, mirroring the main light theme's formula. All six series slots are official DESY colours drawn from the palette's dark half so they stay legible against a near-white plot area (cyan 4.21, orange 2.90, green 3.03, dark-red 5.59, aubergine 6.42, purple 6.63). Series 2 inherits the accent-secondary shortfall — as a line/marker colour it is held to the 3:1 non-text tier and sits just under it.

theme.$description: Must exactly match an asset 'name' in src/osprey/interfaces/vendor_manifest.json (contract-tested).
